verdicts.reason: S2 supports one rule per collection, multiple archives per namespace with one active, no multiple archives on the same fields, 50/20 limits, the Flex exclusion and the Infinite public-preview exclusion. S1 and S3 support namespace immutability in the UI and the API note on Paused/Deleted archives. S6 also states the Flex and Infinite exclusions.

S1 documents Date Match (indexed date field plus days) and Custom Criteria (find filter, empty document rejected), and says the date field cannot be changed. S3 documents timeField plus days, ISODate format, full bucket documents only, and that the time field cannot be changed. S6 confirms the empty document is rejected.

The days kept on the cluster and the optional separate retention period are documented in both creation guides. By default Atlas does not delete archived data. S6 shows Age Limit and Deletion Age Limit as separate settings. The scope note disclaims API and CLI detail.

S6 says Age Limit and the custom query can be modified via the UI and API, and gives the CLI update command. Its UI edit steps cover deletion age and schedule. Switching Date Match and Custom Filter is disallowed. Partition fields and structure cannot be modified via the UI or API, and the $merge migrate/rehydrate, delete and recreate workaround is documented. The claim's caveat about uneven API/CLI coverage is accurate.

S2 supports the five-minute task cadence, the 100 MB per file and 2 GB per cycle limits, the five-minute wait after a job, the 7-day and 5 MiB behavior, and the inconsistent-snapshot risk. S1 and S3 support the PENDING status when a node is down.
S1 and S3 give 7 to 9125 days, the 24-hour delay and unrecoverable deletion. S6 shows Deletion Age Limit and says an empty field disables the rule. The scope correctly limits this to the UI.

S4 and S5 both state expire_after_days in the Data Expiration Rule must be between 7 and 9215, which differs from the UI's 9125. The claim correctly says the enforced limit is not established and that the sources are unpinned documentation.

S6 supports the five-day delay and Deleted state, cluster deletion removing archives, dropped database or collection leaving archived data with storage cost, and the Orphaned state for a deleted or resharded collection with no automatic removal.

The optional toggle over the default periodic runs, daily/weekly/monthly frequency, the two-hour minimum and the 29th-31st skip (February example in S1 and S3) are all documented. No catch-up run is described, which the claim states only as an absence.

S1 and S3 say a running job continues until complete. S6 says editing the schedule does not interrupt a running job and the setting takes effect after it completes, that disabling returns to the default periodic job, and that the Schedule column shows the next window on hover.

Both provider pages list DAILY/MONTHLY/WEEKLY, start and end hours and minutes, day_of_month for MONTHLY only, and day_of_week for WEEKLY only with Monday 1 and Sunday 7. The example uses equal start and end values. The pages do not state a two-hour minimum, and the claim does not assert one.

Both pages state create/edit/pause/resume, the required arguments, that the collection must exist, collection_type TIMESERIES or STANDARD with default STANDARD, type must be DATE for TIMESERIES, and the DATE criteria note requiring date_field among the partition fields.

S4 and S5 document the pending-forever behavior with a missing date_field, the ONLINE_ARCHIVE_CANNOT_MODIFY_FIELD error, and the immutability of data_process_region. They are silent on db_name and coll_name changes. S1 states the UI namespace cannot be modified.

The paused argument and resume failure, sync_creation default false waiting for IDLE or ACTIVE, the 3h create timeout, delete_on_create_timeout default true, the hyphen-joined import ID and the listed states are all in S4 and S5. S6 corroborates the state names within the same evidence origin.

Both pages carry the same passage: an index sufficiency query during the first run, a scanned-to-returned ratio of 10 or more triggering the warning, and possible value conversion for custom expressions. The claim treats the two copies as one vendor statement.

S1 requires an index on the Date field and warns that $expr may prevent index use. S3 recommends a compound index on control.closed and control.min.<date_field>. Both guides have explain and index-creation steps, and the claim keeps the collection-type scope.

Both pages say the check stops once sufficient indexes are detected and that no warning is issued if an index is dropped later. The conclusion about absence of the warning is clearly marked as an inference and is consistent with the sources.

notes: All sources are one MongoDB vendor-documentation origin, so SUPPORTED verdicts are not independent corroboration.
S4 and S5 are unpinned; the v2.19.0 examples-link tag does not date the provider documentation.
The 9125 (UI) versus 9215 (provider) conflict is documented in the sources themselves and is represented accurately in DE1 and DE2.
